newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg doesn't favour flexible EMU - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg doesn't favour flexible EMU - spokesman.

text.p: A spokesman for Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg denied on Wednesday that Duisenberg was willing to accept a flexible interpretation of the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union.
Earlier on Wednesday NOS radio had reported that Duisenberg would prefer a flexible interpretation of the EMU entry criteria rather than a delay in the January 1999 launch date.
NOS said Duisenberg had made remarks to that effect at a closed meeting of members of parliament of Prime Minister Wim Kok's Labour Party (PvdA) two weeks ago.

But central bank spokesman Bert Groothof told Reuters that while EMU had been discussed at that meeting, Duisenberg had not expressed a preference for a flexible interpretation of the entry criteria which include a ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) for national public sector deficits.
In public statements, Duisenberg and other top Dutch public officials have always called for a strict interpretation of the EMU entry criteria.
Duisenberg is set to take over in July as head of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of the European Central Bank.

Separately, incoming Dutch central bank head Arnout Wellink told a conference of business leaders it was uncertain whether next week's European summit would agree on the EU's budgetary Stability Pact, although he believed it would soon be endorsed.
Wellink said it had been expected important decisions about economic and monetary union (EMU), including the stability pact would be taken at the summit.

"As things stand now, however, due to political and domestic reasons, it is uncertain whether agreement could be reached at the summit in Amsterdam," he said, adding, however, he did not think it was impossible. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
